title: Verifying the Java Installation
subtopics: Confirming that the correct JDK is being used
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of verifying the java installation and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—checking the java runtime version—in a small, readable example.
Predict the example result and check it against the stated output or a boundary-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study verifying the java installation with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you make sure your terminal and editor use the JDK you intend to learn and build with. In this lesson, focus on checking the java runtime version and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Use the standard library type that matches the data: java.time for dates and zones, BigDecimal for exact decimal arithmetic, and locale-aware APIs for user-facing text and numbers. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect checking the java runtime version with checking the compiler version before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Checking the Java runtime version
items.text: Use the standard library type that matches the data: java.time for dates and zones, BigDecimal for exact decimal arithmetic, and locale-aware APIs for user-facing text and numbers.

items.title: Checking the compiler version
items.text: Use Path and Files for modern file operations, choose byte or character APIs based on the data, and close resources reliably. Parse external files defensively because their contents may be incomplete or malformed.

items.title: Confirming that the correct JDK is being used
items.text: The JDK supplies the Java compiler and development tools as well as a runtime. A runtime can execute applications, but compiling and debugging usually require the JDK tools.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect the runtime selected by the current java command. For ordinary Java SE examples, use JDK 25, save a complete class as Main.java, and run `javac Main.java` followed by `java Main`. CodeLeaf does not execute Java in the browser; use a local JDK for these examples. Preview-only and configuration-file examples have their own version or filename notes.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the original example, remove any temporary output files it created, and rerun the baseline case. Do not leave credentials, generated private data, or large test files in the project directory.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

content.task: Try it yourself: verify your local JDK and editor setup for verifying the java installation. Record the relevant command output, then explain what each result proves. Do not change global environment settings until you know which JDK your terminal is using.
